selected_problem: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. Fresh-main inspection found that extensionless relative-import edges used the first repository path whose prefix matched the import. Repository input order could therefore make `./foo` resolve to `foo.test.js` instead of `foo.js`, contaminating semantic centrality and context selection with an incorrect dependency edge.

execution.route_basis: The fresh canonical main exposes one narrow, deterministic semantic-graph defect with a direct wrong-edge reproduction. Source-contract replay therefore narrows the unresolved synthesis boundary to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without prescribing a new module-resolution architecture or forcing mode rotation.

changes: Relative import candidates are now ranked deterministically instead of taking the first input-order prefix match.
Resolution prefers an exact path, then a direct extension-bearing file candidate, then an index candidate; equal-rank candidates are ordered by shortest path and lexical order.
The change is intentionally limited to the existing heuristic semantic graph and does not claim full runtime module-resolution equivalence.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED against fresh main: with `src/foo.test.js` before `src/foo.js`, `src/main.js` importing `./foo` produced an imports edge to `src/foo.test.js` rather than `src/foo.js`.

truth_boundaries: Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED. This removes one input-order-sensitive relative-import ambiguity; it does not implement full Node, TypeScript, bundler, Python, or other language module resolution.
Package exports, tsconfig path aliases, extension priority rules, platform-specific suffixes and non-relative imports remain outside this heuristic semantic graph resolver.
Semantic-context neighborhood selection remains bounded and does not prove globally optimal context selection for arbitrary software goals.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
